correctness.rationale: The strict subcritical compactness theorem applies after choosing an intermediate exponent \(\alpha_0\) with \(\alpha<\alpha_0<1-j/m\), and Hilbert interpolation identifies its target with \(D(B^{\alpha_0})\). The cited endpoint theorem gives boundedness at \(1-j/m\). For an arbitrary fixed compact-resolvent \(B\), an orthonormal eigenbasis with eigenvalues \(\beta_n\to\infty\) and the normalized modes \(u_n(t)=\beta_n^{-1}e^{i\beta_n^{1/m}t}e_n\) have constant graph norm. Their target norms are proportional to \(\beta_n^{\alpha-(1-j/m)}\), and at the endpoint distinct images stay a fixed positive distance apart. This proves noncompactness and supercritical unboundedness for each fixed operator, not merely for a model example.
correctness.risk: The proof is restricted exactly as claimed to finite time intervals and self-adjoint compact-resolvent Hilbert scales; no finite computation is used.

final_claim: For every infinite-dimensional Hilbert space with a positive self-adjoint compact-resolvent operator \(B\ge I\), the same-Morrey map by the \(j\)-th time derivative has exact fractional-domain threshold \(\alpha=1-j/m\): compact below it, bounded but noncompact at it, and unbounded above it.
limitations: No claim is made for non-self-adjoint sectorial scales, pointwise-in-time target topologies, or fractional exponents outside the stated interval.
Older abstract interpolation terminology remains the main originality-search residual risk.
